text.p: Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Monday that Moody's Investor Services, which has resisted raising Argentina's sovereign credit rating, was too "backward-looking" in its assessments.

Credit-rating agency Standard & Poor's raised Argentine long-term sovereign foreign currency debt ratings in March, but Moody's said in April that Argentina's country risk had not fallen enough to merit an upgrade.
Moody's cited the ratios between debt, debt servicing costs and exports. But Fernandez told foreign correspondents:
"I don't share the use of these ratios as the basis for a rating. I believe Argentine risk continues to be high because they are using measurements that are backward-looking."

Moody's lead Argentine analyst Kristin Lindow said earlier this month that Argentina's total debt was equivalent to 373 percent of exports, compared with an average 149 percent for all speculative-grade countries rated by Moody's.
